original_question: Let T be the class of open tau-covers of X (large covers with the finite-comparison condition on membership asymmetry for each pair of points). Is Omega choose Gamma equal to Omega choose T?
target_in_paper: Section 7.1, Problem 7.1: the paper’s “most important problem concerning τ-covers,” namely whether Ω choose Γ equals Ω choose T.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the target comparison and correctly describes T as the class of open τ-covers via the largeness condition plus the finite asymmetry condition for each pair of points. It is aimed at exactly the official problem stated in the paper.
missing_details: The notation “Ω choose Γ” and “Ω choose T” must be defined: for collections U,V of covers of X, “U choose V” means that every cover in U contains a subcover belonging to V.
The ambient class of spaces should be specified as in the paper: X is a set of real numbers (equivalently, a zero-dimensional separable metrizable space).
Ω should be defined explicitly as the family of open ω-covers of X: every finite F⊆X is contained in some member of the cover.
Γ should be defined explicitly as the family of open γ-covers of X: the cover is infinite and each x∈X belongs to all but finitely many members.
The paper’s standing convention that covers are nontrivial should be included: X itself is not a member of the cover.
The definition of a τ-cover should explicitly include largeness: every x∈X belongs to infinitely many members of the cover.
The equality should be stated as equality of properties/classes of sets of reals, i.e. for every such X, X satisfies Ω choose Γ if and only if X satisfies Ω choose T.
refined_question: For a set of real numbers X (equivalently, a zero-dimensional separable metrizable space), let Ω be the family of nontrivial open ω-covers of X, Γ the family of nontrivial open γ-covers of X, and T the family of nontrivial open τ-covers of X, where an open cover U of X is an ω-cover if every finite F⊆X is contained in some U∈U, is a γ-cover if U is infinite and each x∈X belongs to all but finitely many members of U, and is a τ-cover if U is large (each x∈X belongs to infinitely many members of U) and for every x,y∈X either {U∈U : x∈U and y∉U} is finite or {U∈U : y∈U and x∉U} is finite. Is the subcover property Ω choose Γ equal to Ω choose T; that is, does every open ω-cover of X contain a γ-subcover if and only if every open ω-cover of X contains a τ-subcover?
equivalent_formulation: Does every open ω-cover of X contain a γ-subcover exactly when every open ω-cover of X contains a τ-subcover?
justification: The draft matches the survey’s Section 7.1 on τ-covers. There the paper defines τ-covers, sets T to be the collection of open τ-covers, notes Γ⊆T⊆Ω, and then states Problem 7.1 exactly as the question whether Ω choose Γ equals Ω choose T. To make the question stand alone, one must add the meaning of the “choose” notation, the definitions of Ω and Γ, the nontrivial-cover convention, the largeness part of the τ-cover definition, and the paper’s ambient scope of sets of reals. The nearby context also shows that the problem should remain at the subcover level (not be broadened to neighboring S1 or Sfin questions): the survey records the partial result Ω choose T implies Sfin(Γ,T), and the foundational τ-cover paper defines the choose-notation and proves that S1(Ω,Γ)=Ω choose Γ, which explains why the left-hand side should stay in the subcover form used in Problem 7.1.
